title: GPU checkpoint storage tiering: IaC spec and operational runbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary

This document defines the GPU checkpoint storage tiering design, the Terraform/IaC module interface for lifecycle hooks, and an operational runbook for migrations and incidents. It standardizes when checkpoints are kept on local NVMe vs object storage, how replication and cross-region reads are handled to minimize egress, and the IaC patterns teams should use to opt into tiering policies.

Goals
- Reduce per-tenant egress and storage cost by tiering checkpoints according to age and restore probability.
- Ensure restore latency SLOs for live inference and long-tail recount scenarios.
- Provide an IaC-friendly module with clear lifecycle hooks (pre-provision, pre-drain, post-drain, cold-archive).
- Enable safe rollout and fast rollback for storage-policy changes across regions.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: GPU-backed inference services and the associated KV/checkpoint artifacts (model KV caches, attention state snapshots, session-level checkpoints). Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters.
- Non-goals: Deep data governance (PII classification), KMS key design (refer to security-and-compliance for KMS patterns).

High-level architecture
1) Fast local tier: ephemeral NVMe attached to GPU workers. Used for active session checkpointing and low-latency restore (target RTT <= 20ms). TTL: 0–4 hours depending on workload.
2) Warm object tier: region-local object storage (S3-equivalent). Used for restores with soft latency SLO (RTT <= 250ms). TTL: 4 hours–7 days.
3) Cold archive: cross-region replicated object storage (replicated after policy triggers). Cost-optimized, eventual restore (RTT >= 5s to 30s depending on retrieval API). TTL: > 7 days or manual archive.

Decision table (when to move)
| checkpoint_age | restore_probability | primary_tier | retention_policy |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 0–15m | >= 0.8 | NVMe | keep-on-node; never auto-evict while node is active |
| 15m–4h | 0.2–0.8 | NVMe -> Warm | background copy to object store; keep local copy for 30m after copy |
| 4h–7d | 0.01–0.2 | Warm | lifecycle rule -> cold after 7d |
| >7d | <0.01 | Cold | move to archival class or cold region; retention governed by tenant policy |

Metric-driven triggers
- Restore probability is estimated by workload classification (online inference, batch eval, nightly replay). Teams should supply a probability hint when creating a checkpoint. If omitted, system uses default profile per tenant-class.
- Cost threshold: if monthly object egress for restores > 5% of tenant bill, auto-balance read-replicas to region of highest read rate.

IaC module design (terraform module interface)
- Module name: redwood_gpu_checkpoint_tiering
- Responsibilities: create lifecycle policies, S3 bucket(s) with lifecycle rules, IAM roles for copy/replicate jobs, CRON Lambda/Runner jobs for background copying, and hooks for compute node drain.

Required module variables (HCL example)

```hcl
module "gpu_checkpoint_tiering" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/iac//modules/gpu-checkpoint-tiering"

  name_prefix = "tenant-foo"
  primary_region = "us-west-2"
  warm_bucket = "${var.name_prefix}-warm-checkpoints"
  cold_bucket = "${var.name_prefix}-cold-checkpoints"
  replication_regions = ["us-east-1"]

  nvme_retention_minutes = 30
  warm_ttl_hours = 168
  cold_transition_days = 7

  // hooks: ARNs for pre-drain / post-drain webhooks or SQS
  pre_drain_hook = module.node_agent.pre_drain_webhook_arn
  post_drain_hook = module.node_agent.post_drain_webhook_arn
}
```

Lifecycle hooks and recommended semantics
- pre_drain_hook (synchronous): called by node agent before eviction/drain. Reason payload includes: {checkpoint_ids, node_id, active_sessions}. Module should ensure a fast copy of active session state to warm tier within 5s or queue a high-priority copy. If hook returns failure, node drain can be retried or aborted based on drain policy.
- post_drain_hook (async): notifies copy jobs to promote warm copies to region-local read replicas, mark local NVMe metadata as orphaned, and schedule NVMe erasure.
- cold_archive_hook (batch): invoked by scheduled job when moving objects to cold tier; useful for tagging, billing updates, or notifying compliance.

Operational runbook: common scenarios
A. Incident: sudden spike in restore egress leading to billing alert\1. Triggered alert: monthly-tenant-egress > budget_threshold (default 5% of tenant bill)\2. Pager: infra-oncall + tenant-account-owner\3. Triage steps:\   a) Query metrics: s3_get_bytes_by_region, restore_rate_by_tenant, last_checkpoint_age_histogram\   b) Identify hotspots: run analytics to identify tenant prefixes and source region\   c) Mitigation: enable read-replica in same region as highest read-rate via Terraform var toggle (see quick toggle below) or temporarily enable short-lived CDN edge caching for warm reads.\4. Postmortem items: update workload restore probability profile; set soft limits or additional caching for noisy tenants.

B. Incident: node drain caused lost checkpoint (local NVMe removed before copy)\1. Pager: node-owner + storage-platform\2. Triage:\   a) Check pre_drain_hook logs (module logs) for copy failures\   b) If warm copy exists, restore from warm bucket; if not, escalate to restore-simulation team.\   c) Add compensating controls: enforce synchronous copy for session_count > configured threshold (default 25 sessions) and fail drain for < 30s remaining.\3. Rollback/compensate:\   - Recreate node with previous image and attempt local disk recovery (only if forensic window < 120s and node still available).\   - Otherwise use last warm snapshot and accept partial restore.

Quick toggle for emergency read-replica enable\- Update Terraform boolean variable `enable_region_replica` and run `terraform apply -target=module.gpu_checkpoint_tiering.aws_s3_bucket_replication`\- CLI example: `cd infra/iac/tenants/tenant-foo && terraform plan -var='enable_region_replica=true' && terraform apply -var='enable_region_replica=true' -auto-approve`

Monitoring and SLOs
- Restore latency SLOs: NVMe (p50 <= 10ms, p95 <= 30ms), Warm (p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 350ms), Cold (p50 <= 5s, p95 <= 30s).\- Availability goals: 99.95% for warm-tier reads in-region; 99.9% cross-region.\- Alerts:\  - warm_read_error_rate > 1% for 5m\  - background_copy_failure_rate > 0.5% for 15m\  - monthly_egress_percent > 5% -> billing pager

Telemetry and cost attribution
- Each checkpoint object must carry these tags/metadata: tenant_id, tenant_class (dev/staging/prod), restore_probability_hint, created_by, created_at.\- Billing exports augment object tags with restore_count and bytes_transferred; export fed to billing-lambda to attribute reconstruct costs per tenant.

Security and compliance notes
- All warm/cold buckets must be encrypted at rest and enforce TLS-only PUT/GET. Use tenant-scoped KMS keys where required by contract.
- Replication to other regions requires matching KMS policies. See security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth for KMS patterns.

Testing and rollout plan
1) Module integration tests: run unit-level mock S3 tests + e2e canary that performs: create checkpoint -> trigger pre_drain -> ensure warm copy within 5s.
2) Canary rollout: start with single tenant in us-west-2, monitor metrics for 72 hours.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% of tenants over 10 days with rollback gates: copy_failure_rate < 0.5% and warm_restore_latency p95 < 350ms.

Rollback checklist
- If copy failure or restore latencies exceed gates:\  - Flip `enable_tiering=false` in Terraform for affected tenant prefix\  - Re-run `terraform apply` and trigger on-demand rehydration jobs to keep NVMe warm for active sessions\  - Notify tenant owners and schedule postmortem

Implementation notes and known tradeoffs
- Local NVMe provides best latency but is fragile on preemption; rely on short synchronous copies for critical sessions.\- Moving everything to warm tier increases egress and read latency; tiering balances cost and SLOs by age and probability.\- Cross-region replication reduces egress for global reads but increases storage cost; use analytics to place replicas only where read rate justifies cost.

```

  "job_id": "copy-20260210-0001",
  "source": "nvme://node-41/tmp/checkpoints/ckpt-abc123",
  "destination": "s3://tenant-foo-warm/2026/02/10/ckpt-abc123",
  "priority": "high",
  "checksum": "sha256:...",
  "restore_probability_hint": "0.72",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10T12:01:02Z"
}
```
